items.title: Javon Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I think that this most recent situation, murder of George Floyd, has ignited in a way that I’ve never seen...

ctx.x: It makes me wonder if historians or even ten years from now, when they think of the spring of 2020, we already had a political crisis going on, at least in my estimation, and we have a pandemic, and now we have this racial crisis spawned by this incident in Minneapolis. And I don’t have a question here I guess I’m just wondering if you think that this particular time will result in some significant change.

I think that this most recent situation, murder of George Floyd, has ignited in a way that I’ve never seen, and even if you look at a lot of the protests, and most of all I’ve found all the protests in the past that have erupted from cities have been because of the police or the killing of a black person. So you see it over in parts of Europe or London, so it has really spread in a way that you would have never seen it before. And I think that some of the things I’m seeing — I saw something last night on the road…

about 11:30, 11:35, and within about three minutes, five minutes, someone knocked on my windshield. And I looked to my left, it was a policeman. He said, “I’m just getting a response from one of the stores in this area” it was like a little mall, “that you’ve been sitting here for a few minutes. Could I ask why?” I said, “Well it’s really none of your business.” He says, “Well I want to see your driver’s license and registration.” So I had a couple of choices. Because we always have a choice. I could make a big…
